title: “Once I Was Given the Blueprint, Couldn’t Nobody Stop Me”: Postrelease Quality of Life and Reentry Barriers of People Sentenced to Life in Prison as Children
abstract: This study investigates the postrelease quality of life and reentry barriers among people sentenced to juvenile life and long sentences and then released. Findings are reported from a cross-sectional mixed-methods study, drawing on quantitative ( N = 78) and qualitative ( N = 46) data from a sample of people released from prison following a life or long sentence starting before the age of 18. Quantitative results indicate that more unmet reentry needs were associated with diminished well-being. Qualitative data illustrated the connection between reentry needs and quality of life, providing rich descriptions of how participants understood quality of life. Three major themes emerged: (1) “where to begin?”: barriers to reentry; (2) “my worst day out here is still better than my best day in prison”; and (3) “I’m not entitled to freedom.” Postrelease quality of life was shaped by both personal resilience and systemic oppression that continually constrained individuals’ freedom.
